items.title: US stock futures slide as Iran war enters fifth week

featured_image.name: The S&P 500 could join other U.S. benchmarks in a correction next week. Here's what's ahead

items.description:
US stock futures dropped on Sunday night as investors grappled with the economic fallout of the Iran war and braced for a critical jobs report at the end of a holiday-shortened trading week.

Dow Jones Industrial Average futures slid more than 300 points, or 0.7%, late Sunday, while S&P 500 futures fell 0.7% and Nasdaq-100 futures dropped 0.8%, according to MarketWatch. The declines followed a bruising Friday session that pushed the Dow into correction territory — a drop of at least 10% from a recent high — joining the Nasdaq, which had already crossed that threshold. The S&P 500 closed at its lowest level since last July.[1]

items.title: Trump claims progress on Iran peace plan as Tehran denies any talks

featured_image.name: Iran has received Trump's 15-point plan to end war, report says

items.description: President Donald Trump claimed Sunday that Iran has agreed to "most" of the demands in a 15-point peace proposal the United States delivered through Pakistani intermediaries, describing talks aimed at ending the month-old war as going "very well." But the assertion was swiftly contradicted by Iranian officials, who denied any negotiations are underway and accused Washington of pursuing surrender terms disguised as diplomacy.

items.title: Pakistan offers to host U.S.-Iran talks after Hormuz summit

featured_image.name: Will host US-Iran talks in coming days: Pakistan after meeting with ...

items.description: Foreign ministers from Turkey, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia gathered in Islamabad on Sunday for talks aimed at ending the month-old war between the United States and Iran, with discussions centered on proposals to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to global shipping.

items.title: Trump says Iran agreed to let 20 oil ships pass through Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Trump claims coalition to send war ships to reopen strait of Hormuz

items.description:
President Donald Trump said Sunday night that Iran had agreed to release 20 more cargo ships carrying oil through the Strait of Hormuz beginning Monday morning, in what the president called a "sign of respect" and evidence of Tehran's willingness to negotiate an end to the war.[1][2]

Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One as he flew back to Washington, Trump offered a largely optimistic view of the state of talks with Iran, claiming Tehran had agreed to "most of the points" in a 15-point ceasefire proposal the United States delivered through Pakistan. "They're going to give up nuclear weapons. They're going to give us the nuclear dust," Trump said, referring to Iran's stockpiles of enriched uranium. "They're going to do everything that we want to do."[2]

items.title: Oil tops $100 as Houthis join Iran war, threatening Red Sea route

featured_image.name: Experts weigh potential scenarios for oil if Strait of Hormuz closes

items.description:
Crude oil prices climbed sharply as the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran entered its fifth week, with Houthi rebels in Yemen opening a new front by launching missile attacks on Israel and raising fresh fears over global energy supply routes.

U.S. oil futures rose to above $100 a barrel on Sunday, while Brent crude climbed above $114, according to Fortune futures data. The gains extended a week in which May WTI crude surged 5.46% on Friday alone, closing near $100 a barrel, and Brent crude reached $107.81 earlier in the week. Oil prices have risen roughly 50% since the war began on February 28.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Israeli police bar patriarch from Holy Sepulchre on Palm Sunday

featured_image.name: Israeli police block Catholic cardinal from Holy Sepulchre on Palm ...

items.description:
Israeli police on Sunday barred Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem, from entering the Church of the Holy Sepulchre to celebrate Palm Sunday Mass, marking what church leaders called the first time in centuries that the ceremony could not be held at one of Christianity's holiest sites. The incident drew swift condemnation from world leaders, the Vatican, and even the U.S. ambassador to Israel.

According to the Associated Press, Pizzaballa and Father Francesco Ielpo, the custodian of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, were walking privately toward the church — without any procession or ceremony — when Israeli police stopped them and forced them to turn back. Israeli police said they had informed the church on Saturday that no Mass would be permitted, citing safety concerns tied to the ongoing war with Iran, the inability of emergency vehicles to navigate the Old City's narrow streets, and insufficient bomb shelters.[1][2]

items.title: Iran warns U.S. ground troops would be 'set on fire' as diplomats push for talks

featured_image.name: Iran warns U.S. ground invasion would see troops “set on fire,”  state media reports

items.description:
As the U.S. war with Iran enters its fifth week, the Trump administration is weighing increasingly aggressive options that could put American boots on the ground in Iran, including operations to seize the country's enriched uranium stockpile and its critical oil export hub on Kharg Island.

Iran's parliament speaker warned the United States on Sunday against a ground invasion, threatening to escalate attacks on American allies, according to CBS News. The warning came as foreign ministers from Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt convened in Pakistan to push for a diplomatic end to the conflict, even as fresh airstrikes hit Tehran over the weekend.[1][2][3]

items.title: Brent crude tops $116 as Houthi attack widens Middle East conflict

featured_image.name: Strait of Hormuz crisis explained: What it means for global shipping

items.description:
Yemen's Houthi rebels launched their first missile attack on Israel since the start of the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran, sending oil prices sharply higher and raising fears that a second critical shipping chokepoint could be closed off to global trade.

The Iranian-backed group fired a barrage of ballistic missiles at what it described as "sensitive Israeli military sites" in southern Israel on Saturday, triggering sirens around Beersheba and near Israel's primary nuclear research facility. The Israeli military said it successfully intercepted one missile, and no injuries were reported. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree declared the strikes would continue until "the aggression against all resistance fronts" ends.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Comet C/2026 A1 nears fiery solar encounter set for April 4

featured_image.name: When will this sungrazing comet get bright enough to see?

items.description: New Yorkers who look up this April will have no shortage of reasons to marvel. A sungrazing comet hurtling toward a fiery encounter with the sun, the annual Lyrids meteor shower, and NASA's first crewed mission to the moon since 1972 are all converging in a single month of celestial spectacle — though each comes with its own uncertainty.

items.title: Iran vows permanent overhaul of Strait of Hormuz rules

featured_image.name: Twenty countries pledge to secure Strait of Hormuz

items.description: Iran is tightening its grip over the Strait of Hormuz while selectively opening the waterway to allied nations, a strategy that is reshaping one of the world's most vital shipping corridors as the US-Israeli war with Tehran enters its fifth week.

items.title: France arrests two more in foiled Paris Bank of America bombing

featured_image.name: Bomb attack at Bank of America branch in Paris foiled by police

items.description: French authorities have detained three suspects in connection with a thwarted bombing attempt outside Bank of America's Paris headquarters, the country's anti-terrorism prosecutor's office said Sunday. The arrests mark a widening investigation into what officials suspect may be part of an Iranian-linked campaign of attacks on Western interests across Europe.

items.title: Iran threatens Gulf university campuses as strikes pound region

featured_image.name: Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatens US universities in the Middle ...

items.description: Iran unleashed a fresh barrage of missile and drone attacks across Gulf states over the weekend, hitting Kuwait's main airport, Oman's Salalah port, and a key U.S. air base in Saudi Arabia while issuing threats against American and Israeli universities in the region. The strikes, spanning March 27 to 29, mark a continued broadening of Tehran's retaliation one month into the war that began with joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28.

items.title: NASA begins final countdown for Artemis II moon launch

featured_image.name: When is Nasa's Moon mission launch and what will Artemis do? - BBC

items.description: Four astronauts are days away from departing for the moon aboard NASA's Artemis II mission, with liftoff targeted for 6:24 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, April 1, from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. If all goes as planned, it will mark the first crewed lunar voyage since Apollo 17 in December 1972.[1][2]

items.title: Zelensky signs Gulf defense deals as Ukraine-Russia talks remain frozen

featured_image.name: Zelensky agrees defense cooperation with UAE, Qatar on Gulf tour

items.description: The Kremlin is intensifying its calls for the United States to leverage its influence over Kyiv to secure a peace deal favorable to Moscow, as US-brokered negotiations on ending the four-year war in Ukraine remain stalled by the widening conflict in the Middle East.

items.title: Iran warns against ground invasion as diplomats meet in Pakistan

featured_image.name: Pakistan maintains 'delicate balancing act' as it hosts Iran talks

items.description:
Foreign ministers from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt gathered in Islamabad on Sunday for a two-day summit aimed at charting a path toward ending the month-long war between the United States, Israel, and Iran, even as fighting continued and Tehran publicly rejected the terms on offer. Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar is leading the talks, which officials have described as the most coordinated regional diplomatic effort since the conflict began on February 28.[1][2][3]

Neither the United States, Iran, nor Israel is participating in the meetings. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said the goal was to open "direct dialogue" between Washington and Tehran, which have so far communicated only through intermediaries. Turkey's Hakan Fidan and Saudi Arabia's Prince Faisal bin Farhan rounded out the gathering, which Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif set up after holding what he called "extensive discussions" with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Saturday.[3][4][5]

items.title: Satellite images show 88 structures destroyed at key Iran missile site

featured_image.name: Iran ballistic missiles sites severely damaged by U.S., Israeli strikes -  The Washington Post

items.description: A month into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, a Washington Post analysis of satellite imagery published Saturday found that four of Iran's key ballistic missile manufacturing sites have suffered severe damage, with at least 88 structures destroyed at the Khojir Aerospace Complex alone. Yet U.S. intelligence assessments reveal that only about one-third of Iran's missile arsenal has been confirmed destroyed, and Tehran continues to launch missiles across the region.[1][2]

items.title: Netanyahu orders expansion of Israel's ground invasion in southern Lebanon

featured_image.name: Netanyahu: War against Iran 'continuing with full force ...

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced Sunday that Israel will expand its ground invasion of southern Lebanon, ordering the military to broaden what he called the "existing security strip" as fighting with the Iranian-backed Hezbollah militant group enters its fourth week.

"We are determined to fundamentally change the situation in the north," Netanyahu said during a visit to northern Israel, adding that "Hezbollah still has residual capability to fire rockets at us."[1][2][3]

No immediate details were provided on how far the expanded zone would reach.

items.title: Pentagon prepares ground operations in Iran as war enters 30th day

featured_image.name: 2,200 US Marines to arrive in Middle East on March 27 on ...

items.description: Approximately 3,500 U.S. Marines and sailors aboard the amphibious assault ship USS Tripoli arrived in the Middle East on March 27, U.S. Central Command confirmed Saturday, as the U.S.-Israel war against Iran enters its 30th day with mounting signs of escalation. Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf responded with a stark warning, saying Iranian forces "are waiting for the arrival of American troops on the ground to set them on fire and punish their regional partners forever".[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Ukrainian drones crash in Finland, extending NATO airspace breaches

featured_image.name: Two unidentified drones crash in southeastern Finland in 'suspected  territorial violation'

items.description: Two drones crashed in southeastern Finland near the city of Kouvola on Sunday morning, in what the country's defence ministry described as a "suspected territorial violation" — the latest in a string of incidents in which Ukrainian strike drones have veered into NATO territory amid intensifying attacks on Russian energy infrastructure.

items.title: Study pinpoints sun's storm engine 200,000 km below surface

featured_image.name: Visualization of the solar interior with the tachocline | Instituto de  Astrofísica de Canarias • IAC

items.description: Physicists at the New Jersey Institute of Technology have pinpointed the origin of solar storms to a thin boundary layer buried roughly 200,000 kilometers beneath the sun's visible surface, providing the first direct observational evidence that this region drives the star's magnetic activity cycle.
